terms.meaning: An outside library the project needs in order to run.
A rule such as caret that allows newer compatible versions of a library to be installed.
A library needed only for building, testing or checking code, not for running the app.
The testing tool that finds and runs the spec files.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Scripts and runtime libraries
sections.what: Lists the commands for building, running in development, starting the built app, linting, testing and cleaning. Also lists the libraries the API needs while it runs, such as the web framework, database, Redis, storage, and email.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is the standard layout for a NestJS project.
sections.watch_out: Version ranges let libraries change on install, so the lock file must stay committed.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Developer tools and Jest setup
sections.what: Lists the tools used only during development, such as type checking, linting, and test helpers. Sets Jest to find files ending in spec.ts under the source folder and to report coverage.
sections.why: Likely reason: tests live next to the code and use a spec naming pattern.
sections.watch_out: A test file must end in spec.ts or Jest will not run it.

summary: The project manifest that names the API, lists its libraries and commands, and sets up its test runner.
purpose: Tells the package manager which libraries to install and gives short commands to build, run, check and test the API.
why: Standard for a Node.js project. The test setup is visible in the Jest section.
how: 1) The package manager reads the dependency lists and installs them. 2) Developers run named scripts such as build, dev, lint and test. 3) The test runner reads its settings to find and run spec files.
inputs: Commands typed by developers, and the library versions listed here.
outputs: Installed libraries, a built API, lint results and test results.
risks: Version ranges let libraries update when someone installs without the lock file. The lock file is used in the Docker build. Both bull and @nestjs/bull are listed, which may be redundant. This was not verified. The nodemailer version and its type package should be checked for compatibility. This was not verified.
debug: If installing fails, check the lock file and the workspace package links. If tests cannot find modules, check the root directory and module name settings in the Jest section.
